question_text: The U.S. Constitution starts with the words “We the People.” What does “We the People” mean?
lead_in: You only need one — these all point at the same big idea:
disambiguation: All of these mean the same thing in different words: the people are in charge of the government, not the other way around.

why_it_matters.text: These words flipped history. For ages, kings held the power and the people obeyed. “We the People” says the opposite: the government's power comes from regular people — and belongs to them.

fun_fact.text: An early draft of the Constitution started by naming all thirteen states, one by one. A delegate changed it to just three words: “We the People.” That small change meant the country belonged to its people — not to thirteen separate states.
